messages:
Incident Bot: INCIDENT ALERT — high 5xx rate on dedicated-eu-01 (customer: Oceanic Health, tenant: oce-42). Error rate ~18% over 5m, p99 latency spiked. Pager rule matched: severity=production-impact. Paging @oncall-sre.
Amanda Li: I'm on it — grabbing host logs and tailing the runtime. Kicking off the dedicated-cluster failover/rollback playbook.
Ryan Chen: joining. Any infra signals (OOMs, GPU saturation, autoscale events)?
Amanda Li: autoscaler shows pool capacity saturated, several GPUs at 98% utilization. I see a model variant rollout 7m ago: model: openLlama-quant-v2 -> likely KV cache warmup + increased token generation = thrash. Starting immediate rollback to previous variant.
Meera Patel: tagging customer-facing folks. @Jose, can you draft a brief incident notification for Oceanic Health? They have a dedicated SLA and prefer phone-first for >15m impact.
Jose Alvarez: On it. Drafting now — will paste below for quick review.
SupportBot: Customer contact routing for Oceanic Health (per account record):
- Primary SRE: sree@oceanichealth.com, +1-415-555-0123
- Platform Ops: ops@oceanichealth.com, +44-20-5555-0100
- Exec sponsor (CTO): cto@oceanichealth.com
Routing rule: notify primary SRE immediately, escalate to Platform Ops at 15m if unresolved, escalate to Exec sponsor at 30m.
Amanda Li: rollback kickoff at 1719504355. Will post status as we have metrics.
Ryan Chen: rollback script running: 
```
./deploy_ctl rollback --cluster dedicated-eu-01 --model previous-stable --confirm
```
Amanda Li: rollback completed at 1719504460. Immediate telemetry: error rate down to 2%, p99 latency back to baseline. Keeping monitoring for 30m window.
Incident Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — automated: incident status moved to mitigated (rollback complete). Keep thread for comms + RCA kickoff.
Meera Patel: Good. We should send two communications: 1) interim status page update now, 2) customer email + phone call to primary SRE and ops. Drafts below.
Jose Alvarez: CUSTOMER EMAIL DRAFT (please edit):
```
Subject: Incident: Temporary elevated errors for Oceanic Health (dedicated-eu-01) — Mitigated

Hi Team,

We experienced a temporary increase in 5xx errors for your dedicated-eu-01 instance starting at ~2024-12-05 14:12 UTC. Impact: some requests returned 5xx or experienced elevated latency. Scope: affected only requests routed to dedicated-eu-01 (Oceanic Health tenant).

What we did: reverted a model rollout on dedicated-eu-01 that caused cache thrash and high GPU contention. Rollback completed and error rates returned to baseline at 14:21 UTC.

Current status: mitigated, monitoring for regression for 30 minutes.

Next steps: we will conduct an RCA, share findings and timeline for preventive action within 48 hours. If you need immediate assistance, contact our on-call SRE at sree@oceanichealth.com or +1-415-555-0123.

Apologies for the disruption — we know any outage is costly and appreciate your patience.

Regards,
Jose Alvarez
Redwood Inference — Customer Success
```
Amanda Li: minor edit: change time format to UTC and include exact rollback timestamp. Approved otherwise.
Meera Patel: STATUS PAGE UPDATE DRAFT (short):
```
Partial service disruption for Oceanic Health on dedicated-eu-01 — Mitigated
We detected elevated 5xx errors and latency due to a model rollout. We rolled back the model and service has returned to normal. Investigation ongoing. Next update in 1 hour or on resolution.
```
SupportBot: Noting customer SLA: for Oceanic Health (tier: enterprise), incident of this class triggers priority phone outreach and account manager escalation.
Kevin Ortiz: I’m the next on-call for follow-up — acknowledged handoff at 1719504500. I’ll take the RCA lead and dig into kernel selection + KV cache eviction patterns.
Ryan Chen: filing follow-up ticket INF-7891 with attachments (logs + metrics). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7891
Amanda Li: quick mitigation notes for postmortem:
- Trigger: model variant rollout increased token generation, caused KV cache warmup + cache misses -> elevated memory usage and CPU/GPU contention.
- Immediate action: rollback to previous-stable model variant.
- Short-term mitigation: add rollout traffic ramping policy and autoscale buffer to dedicated-eu pools.
- Long-term: improve rollout compatibility checks for cache pressure heuristics.
Meera Patel: Customer notification plan: phone primary SRE now with brief, follow up with email (Jose to send), then ops if >15m. Jose please send phone + email now.
Jose Alvarez: Called primary SRE at 14:23 UTC, left voicemail and followed up with the draft email. Email sent at 14:25 UTC. Copying here for records.
Amanda Li: monitoring window in progress. If any spikes return, we'll revert and open emergency call.
Incident Bot: REMINDER — make sure to pin status page update and include incident link INF-7891.
Kevin Ortiz: Starting deep-dive: steps I'm taking — pull kernel selection logs, KV cache metrics across nodes, and scheduler traces. ETA for preliminary RCA: 24 hours.
Meera Patel: I'll prepare an internal comms blurb for execs and sales (short impact statement, accounts affected list). Draft: 

"Summary: A model rollout caused elevated errors on dedicated-eu-01 affecting Oceanic Health. Mitigated via rollback. No customer data compromise. We are executing an RCA with next update in 24 hours."

Amanda Li: final operational note: add a temporary rule to prevent auto-rollouts onto dedicated pools until we finish the RCA. I will patch deployment controller.
Ryan Chen: noted. Patching rollout controller flag: blocked_auto_rollouts=true applied at 1719504802.
Jose Alvarez: Customer follow-up: offered 10% credit for downtime per SLA; awaiting customer reply.
Amanda Li: thanks everyone. I’m closing the active paging now and handing RCA to Kevin/Ryan. Amanda signing off at 1719504999.
Kevin Ortiz: ack. I’ll post interim RCA notes and keep this thread updated.
Incident Bot: INCIDENT LOGGED — severity: production-impact, resolution: mitigated via rollback. Thread will remain open for RCA updates.
